sentences.text: Few cases of F. vaginae bacteremia have been reported, primarily in the context of pregnancy or gynecological procedures.
Bacterial vaginosis is described as depletion of Lactobacillus species with overgrowth of facultative anaerobic bacteria, particularly Gardnerella spp. and Fannyhessea vaginae.
A study of 152 women reported higher F. vaginae loads in bacterial vaginosis than in normal and intermediate microbiota, with a selective increase in interleukin-1 beta.

Among 100 women undergoing in vitro fertilization in Taiwan, higher levels of bacteria associated with bacterial vaginosis, particularly Fannyhessea vaginae, correlated with implantation failure and early embryonic loss.
